thread:
maya: quick experiment idea — can we reduce header-affinity when picking backup models? I'm seeing tenant headers causing a lot of spillover into expensive lanes :thinking_face:
jonathan: which header specifically? x-tenant-route or x-routing-hint? we use those for sticky cache and warmup so not trivial to change
amanda: +1 on clarifying which header. if we loosen affinity we might lose cold-KV cache hit rate and spike latency for canary tenants
maya: agree about cache hit risk. my thought: only honor header-affinity for primary lanes. for fallbacks, prefer lane-scoped rules (cost/latency tiers) that ignore tenant header unless explicit safelist is set
oliver: that sounds reasonable. fallback selection currently does naive matcher: first header match -> route. it doesn't reason about capacity. we should add a probe score to fallback decision (capacity_score + latency_budget)
jonathan: capacity_score makes sense. also we should detect when affinity causes cascade: sample traces where tenant header forces fallback into a smaller pool that trips CB
maya: attaching a tiny config prototype — it's intentionally minimal to test behavior:
```
route: /v1/generate
matchers:
  - header: x-routing-hint
    type: prefer
    mode: primary_only
fallbacks:
  - name: cost-tier-1
    ignore_headers: [x-routing-hint, x-tenant-id]
    capacity_score_threshold: 0.6
    cb_trigger: 8/min
  - name: backup-small-gpu
    ignore_headers: [x-routing-hint]
    capacity_score_threshold: 0.3
    cb_trigger: 4/min
```
amanda: nice. for telemetry we'll need two new labels: fallback_reason (header_affinity|capacity|cb) and chosen_selector (affinity|tier|probe). add them to request_span tags so console can filter
maya: yeah — console team, we want a quick dashboard: fallback waterfall for selected tenant + heatmap of affinity-triggered vs probe-triggered fallbacks
oliver: UX ask: add a rollout toggle that lets SRE flip "ignore_affinity_for_fallbacks" per route during canary. preview should show estimated percent affected by header-relaxation (based on last 24h traffic)
jonathan: implementation note — keep default false. when true, we should still let tenant safelist bypass and keep affinity if safelist flag set in route metadata
maya: deploy-bot: kick a small feature branch deploy for the experiment env?
deploy-bot: started deployment to infra-experiments namespace (deploy-1728). logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/deploys/1728 :rocket:
amada: (typo) meant amanda: I'll add telemetry plumbing for fallback_reason and chosen_selector. will push a metrics PR and add an alert: if fallback_due_to_affinity > 5% for >10m AND avg_p90_latency increases by 20% -> page SRE
oliver: also recommend adding a short-circuit probe that tries to pre-warm backup pools when affinity would cause cold misses. cheap probe: 1 token generate with low priority to warm KV
maya: perfect. post-mortem note: we should record an example tenant trace if we flip the toggle so product can see UX impact
jonathan: one more thought: CB triggers should be per-lane not global. current CB is tenant-scoped, which means one noisy tenant takes down lane for everyone. change to lane-scoped with backoff windows
maya: ok will open RFC doc for lane-scoped CB + affinity-relax rollout plan. can we convene 30m sync tomorrow? 10:30am PT?
amanda: I'm in
oliver: me too
jonathan: works for me
maya: thanks — I'll drop the RFC link in this thread once created and include the experiment config + expected telemetry fields. :thumbsup:
